sections.heading: Aristotle's Parts of Animals
paragraphs: This is the Greek text of Περὶ ζῴων μορίων (conventionally "Parts of Animals").
This work is a genuine, undisputed work of Aristotle.

The text here is Greek only, verbatim. Nothing is translated, modernised, normalised or silently corrected beyond the documented resolution of the source's own apparatus markup (see "How it was imported" below). Where the source is irregular or a genuine judgement call was made, it is preserved/recorded and flagged in "Known gaps & anomalies" below.

sections.heading: English translation
paragraphs: An English translation of this work is in scope for a separate, concurrently-run import task covering select works of this reader; see this data directory's sibling `-en` work (if present) for its own about.json and provenance. This Greek import does not itself depend on that translation existing.

sections.heading: The edition
paragraphs: Per this XML file's own <sourceDesc>: Aristotelis De partibus animalium libri quattuor (Langkavel, ed., Teubner, 1868), Leipzig, 1868.

A stretch of Book 4 (around the traditional chapters on bird/quadruped locomotion) carries 19 bare `<note>` spans (no `type` attribute - distinct from this file's ordinary `<note type="marginal">` Bekker citations) holding, verbatim, up to ~1.5KB of running Greek prose each, several explicitly labelled in the source itself "editio prior." / "editio posterior (cod. Y)." - i.e. Langkavel's edition preserves TWO parallel variant recensions of this stretch side by side, not a short editorial comment. Discarding them (this importer's default policy for a non-citation <note>) would silently delete real ancient text - one chapter (book-4-ch-12) would end up with zero passages at all, caught by this importer's own raw-vs-imported coverage check. Both variants are therefore kept, verbatim, inline (unwrapped rather than discarded) - meaning this stretch of the reading text visibly repeats similar content in two slightly different phrasings, exactly as the source itself preserves it, rather than this importer silently picking one recension or merging them.

sections.heading: Digital source
paragraphs: The machine-readable text is the TEI XML file tlg0086.tlg030.1st1K-grc1.xml (CTS urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0086.tlg030.1st1K-grc1) from the OpenGreekAndLatin / First1KGreek project. It was fetched once and is bundled with the app (scripts/import-aristotle-rest/raw/tlg0086.tlg030.1st1K-grc1.xml); nothing is loaded from the network at runtime.

sections.heading: How it was imported
paragraphs: The importer's generic TEI walker (scripts/import-aristotle-rest-shared/teiWalker.ts) parses this source's own <div type="textpart" subtype="..." n="..."> nesting into a tree, and shapes.ts folds it onto this app's Division scheme: Book -> Chapter (id `book-N`/`book-N-ch-M`); deeper source nesting below the "chapter" level, if any, is folded into each Chapter's own Passage array rather than adding another Division level.

... (text an editor judged spurious/interpolated, but which the edition still PRINTS, bracketed - the OCT convention) is KEPT verbatim in the reading text, wrapped in square brackets `[...]` (or left unbracketed-but-verbatim on the rare occasion its own printed text already contains a literal bracket, so as not to double them); / keeps the reading and excludes the variant; a bare (no offered) is itself the edition's printed reading and is kept, logged as a crux; ... (an editorial insertion, printed by the edition) is KEPT inline; ... (a modern editorial citation, not Aristotle's own words) is EXCLUDED; / a Bekker-shaped is captured to build Division.ref and removed from the reading prose; any OTHER is discarded entirely (tag and content); a is kept as its literal printed ellipsis text, a contributes no text; ////////<item>/<list>/<cit> (quotations, verse, foreign-language snippets, emphasis, numerals, a quoted work's title, list/table items) are unwrapped - tags stripped, text kept inline as ordinary reading prose, WHETHER nested inside a <p> or printed as a sibling of one (a verse quotation is very often the latter - e.g. this corpus's Empedocles/Homer citations - and is captured as its own implicit paragraph rather than dropped). Every occurrence of all of these except plain milestones/lb/pb is logged in anomalies.json. Entities are decoded and text is NFC-normalised and whitespace-collapsed; the words themselves are otherwise untouched.

In this file: 7 <del> span(s) bracket-kept, 16 <add> insertion(s) kept, 0 bare <sic> crux(es) kept, 0 <choice><sic> variant(s) excluded in favour of <corr>, 0 literal-ellipsis <gap>(s) kept, 0 lacuna <gap>(s) excluded, 0 non-citation <note>(s) discarded.

sections.heading: Reference scheme
paragraphs: Citation is by Book, Chapter, and Bekker page/column range: each Chapter's Division.ref is built from the Bekker citation marks found in its own text, in document order (a single value if only one falls inside it, "<first>–<last>" if more than one); this work spans Bekker 369a–697a in the standard pagination. 14 chapter(s) carry no Bekker mark of their own in this transcription and have Division.ref = null (flagged individually in anomalies.json, not guessed at).

No printed sub-chapter/line-level reference is attempted for any individual Passage (Passage.ref is null throughout); where a source nests a nameable level below its Chapter (e.g. a "section"), that level's own number survives as Passage.n (e.g. "3", or "3.2" two levels down) rather than being discarded.
